title: Heaven without fear
theme: Naciketas describes the heaven he asks about: no fear, no death, no old age, no hunger or thirst, no grief.

words.context: Raṅgarāmānuja: «स्वर्गशब्दः मोक्षस्थानपरः» — the word means the place of release
Śaṅkara: «न च तत्र त्वं मृत्यो सहसा प्रभवसि» — you do not hold sway there

words.role: main verb (subject understood: one who is there)

sandhi.rule: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra: P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः).
ā before a is left unjoined in the text (see the junction listed below).
aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes o: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) with P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).

sandhi_exceptions.note: tīrtvā aśanāyā-: final ā before a is not merged; the text (and Śaṅkara’s quotation of it) keeps the two words apart.

morphology.note: aśanāyā ‘desire to eat’ and pipāsā ‘desire to drink’ (desiderative of pā): a feminine dual dvandva, object of tīrtvā.
ati-√gam with the suffix ḍa (-ga): ‘going beyond’. Śaṅkara: «शोकमतीत्य गच्छतीति शोकातिगः».
Present of bhī (third class, reduplicated). Its subject is not stated: ‘[one] does not fear’.

translation.literal: ‘In the heaven-world there is no fear at all; you are not there; [one] does not fear because of old age. Having crossed both hunger and thirst, gone beyond grief, [one] rejoices in the heaven-world.’
translation.readable: ‘In heaven there is nothing to fear. You are not there, and no one is afraid of growing old. Beyond hunger and thirst, beyond sorrow, one rejoices in heaven.’

syntax: Three short negative statements (no fear, not you, no fear of old age) and one positive one (having crossed hunger and thirst, beyond grief, one rejoices). The subject of bibheti and modate is not named: whoever reaches that world.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara takes it as the heaven-world, free of disease and fear: «स्वर्गे लोके रोगादिनिमित्तं भयं किञ्चन किञ्चिदपि नास्ति». Raṅgarāmānuja says the word here means the place of release: «स्वर्गशब्दः मोक्षस्थानपरः». The Mādhva commentators take heaven as the familiar svarga, where one stays a manvantara before release (see the schools).

ambiguities.topic: na tatra tvam: ‘you are not there’
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara softens it: death does not suddenly prevail there, «न च तत्र त्वं मृत्यो सहसा प्रभवसि». Vedeśatīrtha: there is no death there until the end of a manvantara, «न तत्र मन्वन्तरकालपर्यन्तं मृत्युरस्तीत्यर्थः».

beginner: Naciketas now prepares his second request. Before asking for the fire that leads to heaven, he describes heaven: a place where there is no fear at all, where death has no hold, where no one dreads growing old, where hunger and thirst are left behind and sorrow is passed by. It is a picture of the ordinary hopes of human beings for what lies after death. The Upaniṣad will later look beyond even this, but here the boy speaks of the best that people usually imagine, and asks how to reach it.
analogy: Like a traveller describing the safe harbour before asking for the chart that leads to it.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: A heaven without fear, without death’s power, without fear of age, beyond hunger, thirst and grief. It is the introduction to the second boon, asked in 1.1.13.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: As the familiar heaven, free from fear caused by disease: «स्वर्गे लोके रोगादिनिमित्तं भयं किञ्चन किञ्चिदपि नास्ति», where death does not suddenly prevail, «न च तत्र त्वं मृत्यो सहसा प्रभवसि». The one who reaches it, having crossed hunger and thirst, is beyond mental pain: «शोकमतीत्य गच्छतीति शोकातिगः».

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: Raṅgarāmānuja: yes, the word here names the place of release, «स्वर्गशब्दः मोक्षस्थानपरः», and he defends the claim at length on 1.1.19, reporting the Śrībhāṣya: «स्वर्गशब्देनात्र परमपुरुषार्थलक्षणमोक्षोऽभिधीयते». The Mādhva commentators keep heaven as heaven: Rāghavendratīrtha notes that the repetition of ‘heaven-world’ may show that the ordinary heaven is meant, «नायं लोकः विष्णुलोकः, किन्तु प्रसिद्धस्वर्गलोक एवेति ज्ञापनाय पुनरुक्तिः», citing Madhva’s words «उष्य मन्वन्तरं कालम्» — one stays there a manvantara.

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: aśanāyā and pipāsā are desideratives of ‘eat’ and ‘drink’: the wanting, not the eating. The verse uses the pair as the mark of embodied need; the Chāndogya uses the same pair for the self that is free of them.

advaita.text: The ordinary heaven, the reward of ritual, described in its best colours; it is not yet the knowledge of the self, which only the third boon will bring. «न च तत्र त्वं मृत्यो सहसा प्रभवसि».

visistadvaita.text: Heaven here is release: «अत्रापि स्वर्गशब्दः मोक्षस्थानपरः». Raṅgarāmānuja argues that the immortality ‘enjoyed’ in 1.1.13 and the crossing of birth and death in 1.1.17 cannot be said of the perishable heaven.

dvaita.text: Heaven is the ordinary svarga, where one lives a manvantara («उष्य मन्वन्तरं कालम्», as Rāghavendratīrtha cites Madhva) before release; Rāghavendratīrtha also allows that ‘heaven’ names Viṣṇu’s world, «स्वर्गशब्दितविष्णुलोकस्वरूपमाह».

schools.disagreement: The question is whether svarga means heaven or release. Śaṅkara keeps heaven as the fruit of ritual, below knowledge; Raṅgarāmānuja makes it release itself; the Mādhva commentators keep it as heaven, from which one later passes to release.

parallels.note: The Chāndogya describes the self as free of old age, death, grief, hunger and thirst — the same list Naciketas gives of heaven. The Upaniṣad will move from a place free of these to a self free of them.

contemporary.text: Most of what people work and save for is a smaller version of this heaven: a life without fear, without want, without the dread of old age. The verse names those hopes honestly before the Upaniṣad asks whether any place can fulfil them. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: What would your own ‘heaven without fear’ look like?
reflect.deeper: Is freedom from fear something a place can give, or only a state of mind?
reflect.practice: List three fears that shape your week. For each, notice whether it is about the future or about now.

references.text: Raṅgarāmānuja’s long defence of svarga as release stands in his comment on 1.1.19 (his file number 1.1.20); see the note on that mantra.

flags.note: Whether svarga here is heaven (Śaṅkara, the Mādhva commentators) or release (Raṅgarāmānuja, following the Śrībhāṣya) is disputed and shapes the reading of the second boon.
